easyedit_deviation: batch_tokens capped at 8,192 (EasyEdit default = full 131,072 context). Covariance is a token sum; result identical. Applied to ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit equally.
note: ROME shipped Llama-3-8B config has mom2_adjustment=false (no covariance pass), so the cap is wired but has no effect there; MEMIT/AlphaEdit: layers 4-8, wikipedia 100,000 samples, float32.
rome_sanity: ROME10 = the same ROME setup on the first 10 CounterFact edits (sequential), scored with the identical harness on all three splits
report_disclosures: ROME collapse (2.0% success, -33.6 pp on the held-out set) is consistent with published findings on sequential editing: Gu et al. 2024, "Model Editing Harms General Abilities of Large Language Models" (arXiv:2401.04700); AlphaEdit (Fang et al., ICLR 2025), sequential degradation on Llama3-8B, Fig. 4.
All baselines: EasyEdit code and its shipped Llama-3-8B default hyperparameters, no tuning, no handicap. ROME rewrite_acc 0.346 per EasyEdit's own metric.
